classes.name: Use After Free
classes.description: Memory is accessed through a pointer or reference after the allocated memory has been deallocated.
classes.exclusion_rationale: The language enforces strict compile-time ownership, lifetimes, and borrow semantics with no manual deallocation. The static analyzer verifies zero unsafe blocks and zero FFI reachability.
attack_patterns: Free followed by read access
Free followed by write access
Use after realloc reallocation
Dangling pointer escaping stack or heap scope

classes.name: Out-of-bounds Write
classes.description: The software writes data past the end, or before the beginning, of the intended buffer.
classes.exclusion_rationale: The compiler instruments all slice and index writes with bounds checks, or proves bounds preservation via type invariants. The static analyzer verifies zero unsafe blocks.
attack_patterns: Off-by-one buffer index write
Negative buffer index indexing
Unbounded destination buffer copy

classes.name: Out-of-bounds Read
classes.description: The software reads data past the end, or before the beginning, of the intended buffer.
classes.exclusion_rationale: The compiler instruments all slice and index reads with bounds checks or panics on divergence. The static analyzer verifies zero unsafe blocks.
attack_patterns: Over-read of trailing buffer bytes
Negative indexing into array or slice
Buffer over-read via untrusted length field

classes.name: Double Free
classes.description: The software calls free() on a resource that has already been deallocated.
classes.exclusion_rationale: Single ownership semantics guarantees exactly one drop execution per heap resource. The static analyzer verifies zero unsafe blocks.
attack_patterns: Duplicate free in error handling recovery branch
Aliased pointer double release

classes.name: NULL Pointer Dereference
classes.description: A NULL pointer is dereferenced, leading to segmentation fault or abnormal process termination.
classes.exclusion_rationale: The type system enforces non-nullable references (&T, &mut T) and mandates explicit handling of Option<T>. The static analyzer verifies zero unsafe pointer dereferences.
attack_patterns: Unchecked dereference of lookup or allocation return
Missing sentinel node check in linked structures

classes.name: Integer Overflow to Buffer Boundary
classes.description: Integer arithmetic calculation of buffer size or offset wraps around, producing an undersized allocation or out-of-bounds pointer calculation.
classes.exclusion_rationale: Language checks arithmetic overflow in debug mode and slices panic on out-of-range indexing. The static analyzer verifies all length calculations are checked or saturated.
attack_patterns: Multiplication overflow in element count times size
Addition overflow in offset plus length calculation

classes.name: OS Command Injection
classes.description: The software constructs all or part of an OS command string using untrusted input without proper validation or escaping.
classes.exclusion_rationale: The package does not declare the proc capability. The static analyzer verifies zero process spawning, exec, or shell invocations.
attack_patterns: Command chaining via shell metacharacters (; | & ` $)
Argument injection via whitespace or flags

classes.name: SQL Injection
classes.description: The software constructs all or part of a SQL command using untrusted input without parameterized queries.
classes.exclusion_rationale: The package does not interact with SQL engines or databases. The static analyzer verifies zero SQL query construction.
attack_patterns: Tautology injection (' OR '1'='1)
Stacked SQL queries and comments (-- or /* */)

classes.name: Path Traversal
classes.description: The software uses external input to construct a pathname intended to identify a file or directory located under a restricted directory, but does not properly neutralize traversal sequences.
classes.exclusion_rationale: The package does not declare the fs capability. The static analyzer verifies zero filesystem paths are constructed or opened.
attack_patterns: Directory climbing using ../ and ..\
Absolute path override (/etc/passwd, C:\Windows)
URL-encoded or UTF-8 multi-byte traversal sequences

classes.name: Cross-Site Scripting (XSS)
classes.description: The software receives untrusted input and places it into dynamic web or HTML content without proper validation or encoding.
classes.exclusion_rationale: The package does not declare the ui capability and outputs no HTML/DOM structures. The static analyzer verifies zero UI/DOM sinks.
attack_patterns: Script tag injection (<script>alert(1)</script>)
Event handler injection in attributes (onload, onerror)
JavaScript URI scheme execution (javascript:...)

classes.name: Code Injection / Eval
classes.description: The software constructs all or part of a code segment using untrusted input from an upstream component and executes it dynamically.
classes.exclusion_rationale: Compiled language without dynamic code evaluation or runtime eval primitives. The static analyzer verifies zero dynamic execution mechanisms.
attack_patterns: Injected code evaluation in eval() or Function()
Dynamic script compilation of untrusted strings

classes.name: Improper Output Encoding
classes.description: The software does not properly encode or escape output before placing it into a downstream protocol or format.
classes.exclusion_rationale: Package performs no serialized protocol formatting, or strictly relies on type-safe verified encoders. The static analyzer confirms no raw unescaped protocol sinks.
attack_patterns: Delimiter injection into CSV, TSV, or key-value streams
Control character injection into header lines

classes.name: Log Injection
classes.description: The software receives untrusted input and writes it directly to log files or audit streams without neutralizing control characters.
classes.exclusion_rationale: Package declares no stdout or logging capabilities. The static analyzer verifies zero ambient logging or stream writing.
attack_patterns: Carriage return and newline (CRLF) injection forging log lines
ANSI escape sequences altering terminal display

classes.name: Uncontrolled Resource Consumption
classes.description: The software does not properly control the allocation or consumption of finite resources such as CPU time, heap memory, or file handles.
classes.exclusion_rationale: Pure computation package with static zero-allocation guarantees and linear step bounds (steps <= c*n + d).
attack_patterns: Adversarial input triggering exponential CPU loops
Unbounded allocation of large arrays or buffers

classes.name: Decompression Bomb
classes.description: The software does not properly limit the resources used to decompress data, enabling a denial of service via high compression ratio inputs.
classes.exclusion_rationale: The package does not implement or invoke decompression or archive expansion routines. Verified by static analyzer.
attack_patterns: Zip bomb / gzip bomb / recursive archive expansion
Highly redundant payload producing gigabytes from kilobytes

classes.name: Uncontrolled Recursion
classes.description: The software does not properly control the recursion depth of nested function calls, leading to call stack exhaustion.
classes.exclusion_rationale: The package contains zero recursive function calls, relying exclusively on iterative loops with bounded state stacks. Verified by AST analysis.
attack_patterns: Deeply nested parentheses, arrays, or object structures
Cyclic graph inputs causing infinite traversal recursion

classes.name: Inefficient Regular Expression (ReDoS)
classes.description: The software uses a regular expression engine with non-linear worst-case time complexity, enabling CPU exhaustion on crafted strings.
classes.exclusion_rationale: Package contains zero regular expression usage and has zero regex dependencies. Verified by static analyzer allowlist.
attack_patterns: Catastrophic backtracking on overlapping quantifier patterns (a+)+$
Nested repetition on non-matching suffix

classes.name: Inefficient Algorithmic Complexity
classes.description: The software uses an algorithm whose computational complexity can be degraded from average to worst-case by crafted adversarial inputs.
classes.exclusion_rationale: All algorithms operate in strict linear time O(n) independent of input values. Verified by WIR cost semantics.
attack_patterns: Hash table collision flooding degrading lookups to O(n)
Adversarial quicksort pivot selection degrading to O(n^2)

classes.name: Observable Timing Discrepancy
classes.description: Differences in execution time, memory access patterns, or microarchitectural state vary with secret data, allowing secret extraction via timing side channels.
attack_patterns: Early return on byte mismatch in secret comparison
Secret-dependent memory indexing causing cache line hits/misses
Secret-dependent branching with observable pipeline stalls

classes.name: Use of Insufficiently Random Values
classes.description: The software uses insufficiently random numbers in a security context that requires unpredictable randomness.
classes.exclusion_rationale: Package performs purely deterministic computation and declares no rand capability. Verified by static analyzer.
attack_patterns: Predictable PRNG seed derivation from system timestamp
Truncated state space in random number generation

classes.name: Use of Broken or Risky Cryptographic Algorithm
classes.description: The software uses a cryptographic algorithm that has known mathematical weaknesses or is obsolete.
classes.exclusion_rationale: Package implements no legacy cryptographic ciphers or digests, or only implements modern vetted primitives per specification.
attack_patterns: Collision generation on MD5 or SHA-1
Key recovery on RC4 or single DES

classes.name: Inadequate Encryption Strength
classes.description: The software uses encryption with a key or parameter length that is insufficient for modern computing capabilities.
classes.exclusion_rationale: Package implements no ciphers with configurable sub-standard key lengths; minimum parameter lengths are enforced at compile time.
attack_patterns: Exhaustive key search on sub-128-bit symmetric keys
Factoring of RSA keys below 2048 bits

classes.name: Concurrent Execution Race Condition
classes.description: The software contains a concurrent execution sequence where access to shared state is not properly synchronized.
classes.exclusion_rationale: Package declares no thread capability and uses zero multithreading or concurrency constructs. Verified by static analyzer.
attack_patterns: Data race on unsynchronized shared memory pointer
Inconsistent intermediate state observed by concurrent thread

classes.name: Time-of-check Time-of-use (TOCTOU) Race Condition
classes.description: The software checks the state of a resource before using it, but the resource's state can change between check and use.
classes.exclusion_rationale: Package declares no fs or proc capabilities and has no external state dependencies. Verified by static analyzer.
attack_patterns: File replacement via symlink swap between stat() and open()
Permission change on filesystem object between access check and modification

classes.name: Deserialization of Untrusted Data
classes.description: The software deserializes untrusted data without sufficiently verifying that the resulting data will be valid.
classes.exclusion_rationale: Package contains zero dynamic object deserializers, polymorphic object factories, or reflection dispatch mechanisms. Verified by static analyzer.
attack_patterns: Gadget chain execution during object unpickling or Java deserialization
Type confusion in polymorphic JSON or XML deserialization

classes.name: Prototype Pollution
classes.description: The software receives untrusted input that can modify the prototype attributes of Object in prototype-based languages.
classes.exclusion_rationale: Language does not possess prototype-based inheritance or dynamic object prototype chains. Verified by compiler and analyzer.
attack_patterns: Recursive deep merge on __proto__ or constructor.prototype keys
Path lookup polluting global Object prototype properties
